paper_title: Extended Search for the Invisible Axion with the Axion Dark Matter Experiment
coupling_convention: g_agamma-gamma in GeV^-1 as plotted on y-axis
notes: ADMX Run 1B (arXiv:1910.08638). Cavity haloscope search over 2.81-3.31 ueV (680-790 MHz), extending prior coverage so that DFSZ axion-photon couplings are excluded from 2.66-3.31 ueV at 90% CL. The paper provides no numerical limit table; the exclusion is shown in Fig. 4. Data points above are approximate, computed at the DFSZ coupling level g = (alpha/2pi f_a)*0.75 with f_a*m_a = 5.7e-6 eV * 1e12 GeV, since the text states the search excludes DFSZ couplings across the full range. Actual limits dip slightly below DFSZ but exact values require digitizing Fig. 4. Gaps exist at five mode crossings (Table I: 704.659, 715.064, 717.025, 726.624, 753.844 MHz). Two DM halo models used: Maxwell-Boltzmann (rho=0.45 GeV/cm^3, quoted here) and N-body Lentz model (rho=0.63 GeV/cm^3). | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 53)) | Vision: Traced the lower boundary of the green 'ADMX (This work)' exclusion region in FIG. 4 (fig_04.png), covering ~677-805 MHz (2.80-3.33 ueV). Frequency converted to mass via m[eV]=4.136e-15*f[Hz]. The boundary is a ragged 'sawtooth' typical of haloscope limits; baseline ~2.5-3e-16 GeV^-1 with dips to ~1.8-2e-16 and a steep rise near 800 MHz where sensitivity degrades, merging with the ADMX 2010 (blue) boundary at ~1.2e-15. A gap between ~748-760 MHz (mode crossing at 753.844 MHz, width 12.7 MHz, Table I) has no limit from this work and was omitted. KSVZ line reads ~1.1e-15 at 2.9 ueV, consistent with theory, confirming y-axis calibration.
